column.text: The most important thing in the market right now is positioning, not price. Hyperliquid whale desks are net short $811M in BTC, $698M in ETH, and $159M in SOL, and that hedging pressure is sitting on a tape that has not found a floor. Flows are mixed. BTC spot ETFs took in +$137.3M on Wednesday 28 Oct, though that figure is partial while issuers are still reporting, and the 7-day net is +$198.1M. ETH is the weak leg: Wednesday's partial print is −$21.4M, and the 7-day net is −$287.6M. SOL printed −$5.7M on Wednesday and is −$43.6M over seven days. Macro is explaining the weakness more than offsetting it. The Fed held at 3.75%-4.00% in a 10-2 vote, with Cook and Hammack dissenting for a hike, and Kalshi puts a 78% probability on a December hike. Fear & Greed sits at 51, which reads neutral, so sentiment is not yet capitulating. Our desk stance is restraint. The tape is down-trending, but that alone is not a short signal. Any short needs a mechanism you can point to in the printed blocks, and below conviction 7 it trades at half size. Continuation longs need real proof: rising open interest and price, a reclaim of the 20-day MA, or a negative-funding squeeze. A counter-trend long belongs only at clear support with a catalyst, never as a reflexive dip-buy. The line to watch is $79k. A break there would trigger the heavy long liquidations stacked on the book. Until then, trade the structure, not the headline. Watch whether ETH's seven-day outflow stops before $79k gets tested, because that is where the next move gets decided.
